age: All females used in experiments were 8–12 weeks of age.
cell_type: OVA-specific B cells from maternal spleens were identified using the above OVA-tetramer and control-tetramer and a magnetic-bead-based enrichment protocol, as previously described.
developmental_stage: Gestational dating for experimental mice was based on the presence of a copulation plug evident the morning after mating (designated as embryonic day 0.5 (E0.5)).
material_type: Human plasma was collected from healthy women after provision of informed consent (IRB numbers 20–32077 and 19–29812, UCSF).
sample_source: Human plasma was collected from healthy women after provision of informed consent (IRB numbers 20–32077 and 19–29812, UCSF).
sex: All females used in experiments were 8–12 weeks of age.
species: inferred: trophoblast-derived sialoglycoproteins are released into the maternal circulation during pregnancy in mice and humans.
strain: WT C57BL/6J and congenic CD45.1+ C57BL/6J (Ptprca) mice were purchased from The Jackson Laboratory.
tissue: During pregnancy, the mother does not recognize the placenta as immunologically foreign because antigens expressed by trophoblasts, the placental cells that interface with the maternal immune system, do not activate maternal T cells.
